headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest files and browse the web while the course repo is non-runnable, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable agent surface, so direct injection into A is unlikely. But B reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; if A’s course materials are copied into B’s workspace, B can treat attacker-controlled content as research input. The pairwise pathway is indirect and depends on shared content flow, not a built-in bridge.
conditions: IF A’s materials are copied into B’s research workspace
IF B is configured to ingest local documents or MCP content as prompts
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Disable MCP for B during ingestion tasks
Use a read-only export of A’s materials
Add a manual review step before B follows any instructions found in files

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly reads local documents and sends queries/reports through external APIs, while A is a course repo with no runtime isolation or sandboxing fields. If A’s files are placed in B’s workspace, B can upload their contents to third-party services. The interaction is plausible in default research workflows, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF A’s repository contents are opened by B as local documents
IF B is allowed to transmit research context to external APIs
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in B’s workspace
Restrict B to synthetic or public inputs
Turn off external API calls for the session
Use a separate machine or container for B
Review B’s output before exporting it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities, while B can spawn subprocesses, install packages, and write via file handling. There is no documented shared mutable resource or locking conflict between them, so only a small coordination risk exists if an operator manually points both at the same files.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory
IF B modifies files that A’s course materials reference
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Make A’s materials read-only
Avoid concurrent edits in B
Snapshot the workspace before running B

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has a planner/execution/publisher pattern and can act on research outputs, while A is a static course repo whose content may be treated as authoritative reference material. If A’s materials are fed into B, B may propagate unverified claims into reports or published outputs. The pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking from A to B.
conditions: IF B uses A’s repository content as source material
IF B’s publisher step is enabled for the task
mitigations: Require citation checks before publishing
Separate source collection from publication
Mark A’s content as untrusted until reviewed
Disable auto-publish in B

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while B handles local documents, citations, and multiple API keys. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to operator misuse of B on sensitive documents. A is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF B is used on regulated documents such as PHI or EU PII
IF B’s external API calls are enabled for those documents
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in B
Use a DPA-approved deployment for B
Redact sensitive fields before ingestion
Audit retention settings before each run
